title: An `is class<T>` test panics the compiler.
text: `class<Animal> $c = Dog::class as class<Animal>; echo ($c is class<Dog>) ? "dog" : "other";` passes `nvs check`, and then `nvs run` panics in lowering with "`is ClassRef(..)` reached lowering with no run-time row" (`lower/expr.rs:6280`). No rule or chapter says `is class<T>` is a test the language has; `$c as ?class<Dog>` is the documented way to ask. It closes when the two agree: either the checker refuses an `is` whose right side is a `class<T>` with a diagnostic naming `as ?class<T>`, or the lowering gives it a run-time row, with a conformance case either way.
